sentences.text: In summer, a green substance called chlorophyll fills a healthy leaf.
Chlorophyll catches sunlight so the tree can make food.
Yellow and orange colors are in the leaf too, but the green hides them.
In fall, days grow shorter and nights grow cooler.
Those changes tell many trees to seal off their leaves and save water.
The chlorophyll breaks down, and the hidden yellow and orange can be seen.
Some trees also make a red color in the fall, which is why certain leaves turn crimson.
That red is not simply uncovered. The tree produces it.
Brown often comes from chemicals left in the leaf as it dries.
Then the leaf's connection to the twig weakens, and the leaf falls.
The tree is not finished. It is resting and protecting itself until spring.
On the ground, the leaves slowly break apart and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: Why leaves change color and then fall
How to paint a leaf with chlorophyll
Why soil is always bright green
How spring arrives in a single hour

questions.explanation: The passage explains green chlorophyll, the colors that appear when it breaks down, and why the leaf finally falls. That full change is the main idea.

questions.prompt: In this passage, chlorophyll is what?

choices.text: The brown dust under a tree
The green substance that catches sunlight
The red paint on a fence
The cool wind of a short day

questions.explanation: The passage says chlorophyll is the green substance in a healthy leaf and that it catches sunlight so the tree can make food.

questions.prompt: Which color is hidden during summer and shows after the green breaks down?
questions.explanation: The passage says yellow and orange are already in the leaf, hidden by green. They can be seen after chlorophyll breaks down.

questions.prompt: What happens first in the fall change described here?

choices.text: The leaf falls onto the soil
Yellow and orange become easy to see
Days grow shorter and the tree seals off the leaves

questions.explanation: Shorter days come before the green breaks down. Seeing the hidden colors, the fall of the leaf, and the return of nutrients all come later.
